newsitem.title: INDIA: Head of scandal-hit India finance group arrested.
newsitem.headline: Head of scandal-hit India finance group arrested.

text.p: The chairman of a failed group of Indian finance companies, who was escorted back to India on Sunday from Hong Kong, will be flown to Bombay later on Monday for further interrogation, a federal investigator said on Monday.

Chain Roop Bhansali, who heads the failed CRB group of companies, was arrested on Sunday night when he arrived in the Indian capital accompanied by his family and two officials of the federal Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).

"Bhansali will be flown to Bombay along with a CBI team including joint director M.L. Kumawat. They are expected to get to Bombay by 10.00 p.m. (1630 GMT)," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
Kumawat was the senior CBI official involved in bringing Bhansali back from Hong Kong on Sunday, and is heading the investigations.
"The interrogations will begin in Bombay from tomorrow. We will see how it goes from there," the CBI official said.
Two weeks ago the CBI said it would complete within a month an investigation into the group, whose liabilities are estimated at 9.32 billion rupees ($260 million).

Bhansali fled to Hong Kong on May 13 along with his family, after one of India's leading banks, the State Bank of India, complained to the CBI about the firm defaulting on repayment of a 570 million rupee loan.
The Reserve Bank of India, the central bank, last month charged CRB Capital Markets, which has offices in India and overseas, with a series of irregularities relating to its activities.

The bank also invited claims from investors of CRB Capital Markets for submission to the official liquidator appointed by a local court. A winding-up petition filed by the central bank will be heard on July 22.

"The revelation of the CRB Capital Markets scam...points to a disturbing regularity in frauds visiting the Indian financial system," the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE) said in its May report.
It noted that the CRB scandal has broken five years after a $1.28 billion share scandal that rocked Indian markets.

"The confidence of investors in the primary markets was shaken by the hundreds of companies which raised money with putrid paper -- mostly in 1994-95. Most of such paper is illiquid today," the CMIE report added.
Bhansali's return to India was made possible by the Indian government's approval last Thursday for an agreement between India and Hong Kong for the surrender of fugitives and offenders.
The CBI declined comment on whether Bhansali was the first fugitive to be sent to India from Hong Kong after the approval of the agreement.
Last Thursday the CBI arrested four directors of CRB group companies, a finance controller of the group and a close associate of Bhansali.
